MISSOURI PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION


        CASE NO.: ER-2026-0143




     SURREBUTTAL TESTIMONY

                      OF

              BUCK REUTER

             ON BEHALF OF

     EVERGY MISSOURI METRO




             Kansas City, Missouri
               September 2026
                                   SURREBUTTAL TESTIMONY

                                                  OF

                                           BUCK REUTER

                                       Case No. ER-2026-0143

1    Q:   Please state your name and business address.

2    A:   My name is Buck Reuter. My business address is 818 S. Kansas Avenue, Topeka,

3         Kansas.

4    Q:   By whom and in what capacity are you employed?

5    A:   I am employed by Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. and serve as Manager Regulatory

6         for Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. Missouri Metro (“Evergy Missouri Metro,”

7         “EMM,” or the “Company”), Evergy Missouri West, Inc. d/b/a Evergy Missouri

8         West (“Evergy Missouri West”), Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy Kansas Metro

9         (“Evergy Kansas Metro”), and Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. and Evergy South, Inc.,

10        collectively d/b/a as Evergy Kansas Central (“Evergy Kansas Central”) the

11        operating utilities of Evergy, Inc. (“Evergy”).

12   Q:   Are you the same Buck Reuter who previously filed direct and rebuttal

13        testimony in this case?

14   A:   Yes.

15   Q:   Who are you testifying for?

16   A:   I am testifying on behalf of Evergy Missouri Metro.

17   Q:   What is the purpose of your testimony?

18   A:   The purpose of the Company's surrebuttal testimony is to respond to Staff's

19        position on CS-108 and explain the Company's proposed path forward. While the



                                                                                             1
 1         Company agrees with Staff's recommendation to eliminate CS-108, Staff has

2         expressed concern that the adjustment was established through prior proceedings

3         in Case Nos. EO-2012-0367 and EA-2013-0098 and that the parties to those cases

4         should have an opportunity to be heard. The Company's surrebuttal

5         testimony explains its commitment to addressing that concern by pursuing an

6         amended stipulation in those dockets and providing the original parties, including

7         Staff, OPC, and MIEC, an opportunity to review and comment on the proposed

8         change.

9    Q:   How does the Company plan to address Staff's concern regarding the original

10        parties to the Transource cases?

11   A:   The Company recognizes Staff's concern that all parties to Case Nos. EO-2012-

12        0367 and EA-2013-0098 should have an opportunity to weigh in before the

13        adjustment is eliminated. If the Company files an amended stipulation in those

14        dockets all original parties, including Staff, OPC, and MIEC, will have an

15        opportunity to review and comment.

16   Q:   Does that conclude your testimony?

17   A:   Yes, it does.

                             OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI

In the Matter of Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy       )

STATE OF MISSOURI                       )
                                        ) ss

          Buck Reuter, being first duly sworn on his oath, states:

          1.     My name is Buck Reuter. I work in Topeka, Kansas and I am employed by

Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. as Manager Regulatory.

          2.     Attached hereto and made a part hereof for all purposes is my Surrebuttal

Testimony on behalf of Evergy Missouri Metro consisting of two (2) pages, having been prepared

in written form for introduction into evidence in the above-captioned docket.

          3.     I have knowledge of the matters set forth therein. I hereby swear and affirm that

my answers contained in the attached testimony to the questions therein propounded, including

any attachments thereto, are true and accurate to the best of my knowledge, information and

belief.

                                                Henry S. Reuter
